content: 1. Krishna Swami KV, Somasundaram PR, Tripathy SP, Vaidyanathan B, Radhakrishna S, and Fox W conducted a randomized study comparing two policies for managing default in outpatients collecting pulmonary tuberculosis medications in a large city in South India. This study was published in the journal Tubercle in 1981. 2. Kunawararak P, Pongpanich S, Chantawong S, Pokaew P, Traisathit P, Srithanaviboonchai K, et al. investigated the use of mobile-phone medication reminders to improve tuberculosis treatment adherence in northern Thailand. Their findings were published in the Southeast Asian Journal of Tropical Medicine and Public Health in 2011. 3. Mohan A, Nassir H, and Niazi A explored whether routine home visits improve the return rate and outcomes of DOTS (Directly Observed Treatment, Short-course) patients who delay treatment. Their study appeared in the Eastern Mediterranean Health Journal in 2003. 4. Paramasivan R, Parthasarathy RT, and Rajasekaran S conducted a controlled study on short-course chemotherapy and the effectiveness of an indirect defaulter retrieval method. This research was published in the Indian Journal of Tuberculosis in 1993. 5. Tank ED and Leirer VO examined the role of automated telephone reminders in tuberculosis care, with their findings published in Medical Care in 1994. 6. Moulding TS and Caymittes M studied the management of medication compliance among tuberculosis patients in Haiti using medication monitors. Their research was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2002. 7. Liu X, Lewis JJ, Zhang H, Lu W, Zhang S, Zheng G, et al. conducted a cluster-randomized trial to evaluate the effectiveness of electronic reminders in improving medication adherence among tuberculosis patients. Their study was published in PLOS Medicine in 2015. 8. Bronner LE, Podewils LJ, Peters A, Somnath P, Nshuti L, van der Walt M, et al. assessed the impact of community tracer teams on treatment outcomes among tuberculosis patients in South Africa. Their findings were published in BMC Public Health in 2012. 9. Snidal SJ, Barnard G, Atuhairwe E, and Amor YB evaluated the use of eCompliance, an innovative biometric system for monitoring tuberculosis treatment in rural Uganda. Their study appeared in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2015. 10. Thomson KA, Cheti EO, and Reid T implemented and analyzed the outcomes of an active defaulter tracing system for HIV prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT) and tuberculosis patients in Kibera, Nairobi, Kenya. Their findings were published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene in 2011. 11. Al-Hajjaj MS and Al-Khatim IM reported a high rate of non-compliance with anti-tuberculosis treatment in Saudi Arabia despite a retrieval system, emphasizing the need for directly observed therapy. Their study was published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2000. 12. Broomhead S and Mars M conducted a retrospective return-on-investment analysis of an electronic treatment adherence device piloted in the Northern Cape Province. Their findings were published in Telemedicine and e-Health in 2012. 13. Ngamvithayapong-Y, Anai J, Luangjina S, Nedsuwan S, Kantipong P, Wongyai J, et al. engaged women volunteers of high socioeconomic status to support socioeconomically disadvantaged tuberculosis patients in Chiang Rai, Thailand. Their study was published in WPSAR in 2013. 14. Zou G, Wei X, Witter S, Yin J, Walley J, Liu S, et al. analyzed the incremental cost-effectiveness of improving treatment outcomes among migrant tuberculosis patients in Shanghai. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2013. 15. Lu H, Yan F, Wang W, Wu L, Ma W, Chen J, et al. investigated whether transportation subsidies and living allowances improve tuberculosis control outcomes among internal migrants in urban Shanghai, China. Their study was published in WPSAR in 2013. 16. Wei X, Zou G, Yin J, Walley J, Yang H, Klinner M, et al. evaluated the provision of financial incentives to rural-to-urban tuberculosis migrants in Shanghai as part of an intervention study. Their findings were published in Infectious Diseases of Poverty in 2012. 17. Cantalice Filho JP assessed the impact of providing food baskets to tuberculosis patients at a primary healthcare clinic in Duque de Caxias, Brazil, on treatment outcomes. This study was published in the Journal Brasileiro de Pneumologia in 2009. 18. Sripad A, Castedo J, Danford N, Zaha R, and Freile C examined the effects of Ecuador’s national monetary incentive program on adherence to treatment for drug-resistant tuberculosis. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2014. 19. Tsai WC, Kung PT, Khan M, Campbell C, Yang WT, Lee TF, et al. analyzed the effects of a pay-for-performance system on tuberculosis default case control and treatment in Taiwan. Their study was published in the Journal of Infection in 2010. 20. Bock NN, Sales RM, Rogers T, and DeVoe B explored the use of financial incentives to improve adherence to tuberculosis treatment. Their findings were published in the International Journal of Tuberculosis and Lung Disease in 2001. 21. Safdar N, Hinderaker SG, Baloch NA, Enarson DA, Khan MA, and Morkve O developed a childhood tuberculosis desk guide and monitoring intervention to improve case management in Pakistan. Their study was published in BMC Health Services Research in 2011. 22. Shin S, Livchits V, Connery HS, Shields A, Yanov S, Yanova G, et al. evaluated the effectiveness of alcohol treatment interventions integrated into routine tuberculosis care in Tomsk, Russia. Their findings were published in Addiction in 2013. 23. The World Health Organization (WHO) published the End TB Strategy, outlining global strategies and targets for tuberculosis prevention, care, and control after 2015. This document was released in Geneva in 2014. 24. Floyd K, Hutubessy R, Kliiman K, Centis R, Khurieva N, Jakobowiak W, et al. conducted a systematic review of the cost and cost-effectiveness of multidrug-resistant tuberculosis treatment in Estonia and Russia. Their findings were published in the European Respiratory Journal in 2012. 25. Suarez PG, Floyd K, Portocarrero J, Alarcon E, Rapiti E, Ramos G, et al. assessed the feasibility and cost-effectiveness of standardized second-line drug treatment for chronic tuberculosis patients in Peru. Their study was published in The Lancet in 2002.
